title: Intake orchestration for community weights + variant performance profiling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end, auditable pipeline to intake open-source model weights from community sources, convert them into Redwood runtime-format artifacts, run deterministic validation and multi-slice performance profiles, and publish a signed profile + pinned model version into the model catalog. This ticket focuses on the orchestration and automation glue: staging, metadata extraction, conversion orchestration, profiling job templates, profile ingestion, and automated pinning rules.

Scope and deliverables:
- Staging API: secure S3 staging area + manifest ingestion + provenance checks (hashes, license, declared tokenizer).
- Lightweight preflight: checksum, minimal sample generation (sanity text), tokenizer compatibility check, and declared architecture normalization. Fail fast on incompatible architectures.
- Converter orchestrator: kick off containerized conversion jobs that produce deterministic runtime artifacts (.rmod) with canonical naming (model-name@sha or model-name@semantic-version). Track converter version in metadata.
- Profiling harness: standardized perf suite that runs across a matrix of sequence lengths (32/128/512/2048), batch sizes, and KV cache warm/cold states to produce latency P50/P95/P99 and throughput curves, peak GPU memory, and memory-per-token. Also run quantization compatibility tests for q4/q8 paths.
- Quality validation: smoke generation checks vs baseline prompt set (5 prompts), and embed similarity sanity checks for embeddings-enabled models. Flag models with behavioral regressions.
- Publish step: produce a signed profile artifact (JSON) with keys: pinned_version, converter_version, hardware_profile, kernel_recommendations, fallback_variants. Publish to catalog and optionally create a canary rollout to the dev-serving pool.
- Automation: wire to GitHub Actions + CircleCI staging, with clear failure modes that stop publishing and open a work item for manual review.

Non-goals: full model eval on large benchmarks (GLUE/T0), human-in-the-loop QA for every model (we will triage high-risk licenses or high customer-impact models for manual review).

Decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Coverage vs. profiling time: aim for representative slices (4 seq lengths, 3 batch sizes) to keep CI time bounded while producing useful kernel selection signals.
- Deterministic artifact naming: use content-hash pin to avoid semantic-version drift from community repos while allowing optional semantic tags for user-friendliness.
- Converter runtime version pinned in metadata so runtime can fallback to older kernels if needed.

Success metrics:
- New onboarding run completes end-to-end (ingest -> profile -> publish) unattended in under 90 minutes for a 7B-class model on our standard GPU queue.
- No more than 1 manual intervention per 20 community-model onboards in the first month.
- Profiles include at least 95th-percentile latency and memory metrics and are consumable by the runtime for kernel selection and routing policies.
acceptance_criteria: A secure ingest endpoint exists and stores original weights + manifest in staging S3 with provenance hash
A conversion job template produces runtime artifact and records converter_version in the artifact metadata
Profiling jobs run automatically for matrix slices and produce a normalized profile JSON that runtime can consume
Any failing preflight stops publish and creates a reviewer ticket with the failure log
Successful end-to-end pipeline publishes a pinned catalog entry and a signed profile artifact to the catalog bucket

2026-03-08 — Aisha: Added preflight tokenization checks and minimal generation harness. Noticed one community checkpoint used a legacy tokenizer config — added normalization step. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONB/Model+Ingest+Design

2026-03-10 — Engineering review: Decided to use content-hash pin naming (sha256 of weights+converter-version) to avoid semantic mismatch. Trade-off: less human-friendly but deterministic. Recorded in design doc.

2026-03-12 — QA: Profiling harness runs for 7B model completed on dev GPU pool. Observed pathological memory spike when running cold KV cache for seq=2048, batch=4. Filed follow-up ENG-20735 for runtime memory accounting changes.

2026-03-14 — Miguel: Orchestrator now emits profile JSON with kernel recommendations and fallback_variants. Draft publish step creates catalog entry in dev catalog and triggers canary deploy to dev-serving pool. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/329
